name: Ushigome-Kagurazaka
tagline: Otemachi in 13 minutes and Tokyo in 18 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥120,000 to ¥130,000.
summary: The station is in Shinjuku City, served by Toei Oedo Line. Journey times to the main business districts are 13 minutes to Otemachi, 20 minutes to Shinjuku, 21 minutes to Shibuya and 33 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. The station stands 19 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 18.1 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 19 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 10.8 m to 28.9 m, a difference of 18.1 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of less than 0.5 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 1 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is less than 0.5 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is among the smallest in the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 26 clinics and 20 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is JCHO東京新宿メディカルセンター, about 11 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 神経研究所附属晴和病院, about 13 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Toei Oedo Line.
congestion: Toei Oedo Line runs at 147% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 中井→東中野, which this station is not on. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥120,000 to ¥130,000 and 1K ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. 1LDK ¥210,000 to ¥220,000 and 2LDK ¥350,000 to ¥360,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

Whether it faces a main road or the railway
Whether it sits at the top or the bottom of a slope

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the high side. a small projected flood depth and schools and parks within walking distance pushes the figure up. On the other side, only one line, the {line}, serving the station holds it down. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: For how close the centre is, Kagurazaka; for how little of the area is in the flood projection, Ushigome-Kagurazaka.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Ushigome-Kagurazaka. Kagurazaka has the Tokyo Metro Tozai Line, a different set from Ushigome-Kagurazaka. To Shinagawa, for instance, Kagurazaka is 4 minutes quicker. On how little of the area is in the flood projection, Ushigome-Kagurazaka comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: For rail connections, Iidabashi; for lower rent, Ushigome-Kagurazaka.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Ushigome-Kagurazaka. Iidabashi has 4 lines that Ushigome-Kagurazaka does not. With more lines, Iidabashi is the better connected of the two. To Roppongi, for instance, Iidabashi is 8 minutes quicker. A one-room flat, though, costs about ¥17,000 more at Iidabashi.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
notFor: People avoiding projected flood inundation areas
People who want another route when service is suspended
noiseSources: 大久保通り (1 lanes each way) runs right beside the station, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road
The nearest big road, 早稲田通り, is far enough that little traffic noise reaches the station area

leads.terrain: There are gentle slopes around the station, and which block you live on changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 14 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 2 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Toei Oedo Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the high side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Morning loading on the lines here is about average for the 23 wards' stations.
leads.noiseSources: At this station, check the traffic noise before the noise people make.
